A high-cardinality feature offers many candidate partitions, increasing the chance of finding an apparently good split by noise. A unique transaction ID can isolate rows perfectly while providing no reusable predictive structure. Impurity-based importance inherits related selection bias. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html)

Gain ratio divides information gain by split information, discouraging some high-branching splits but not eliminating all selection bias. Minimum leaf sizes, depth/leaf limits, penalties, and validation reduce memorization. CatBoost's ordered target handling addresses a different but related leakage/prediction-shift problem; it is not simply a cardinality penalty. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.09516)

Audit ID-like variables, compare permutation importance on held-out data, and use group/time splits. A random split can make repeated-entity memorization look useful when deployment must generalize to unseen entities.
